sources.author_or_institution: Rudolf Haag, Jan T. Lopuszanski, and Martin Sohnius; CERN Document Server
sources.title: All Possible Generators of Supersymmetries of the S-Matrix
sources.adaptation_notes: The classification argument and graded-algebra constraints were recast as self-contained matrix, sign, Lorentz-spin, and three-dimensional central-charge exercises. Wording and derivations are original to this edition.

sources.author_or_institution: Philip C. Argyres, University of Cincinnati
sources.title: An Introduction to Global Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: General discussions of the super-Poincare algebra, particle representations, positivity, and R symmetry were reorganized into proofs using the notation and normalizations of Chapter 25. No source solutions were reproduced.

sources.title: Introduction to Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: The algebra, representation, extended-supersymmetry, and BPS themes were separated into new derivational exercises on central charges, massive multiplets, shortening, and parity. Solutions were independently derived in local conventions.

sources.title: Supersymmetric Field Theory
sources.adaptation_notes: Graduate-lecture material on algebra representations, CPT completion, extended multiplets, and BPS bounds was converted into chapter-specific counting and proof problems. Prompts, notation, and all worked solutions were independently written.

sources.author_or_institution: Stephen P. Martin, Northern Illinois University
sources.title: A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.adaptation_notes: The introductory particle-content discussion was used only as a provenance anchor for new helicity-construction exercises on chiral and vector multiplets. The local prompts and solutions were not copied from the notes.

sources.author_or_institution: Philip C. Argyres; University of Cincinnati
sources.title: An Introduction to Global Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: The official four-component graduate notes were used as a provenance anchor for new exercises on general and chiral superfields, Kahler transformations, moduli, discrete transformations, and improved currents. Every prompt and derivation was rewritten in the conventional four-component notation of Volume III.

sources.title: Introduction to Supersymmetry
sources.adaptation_notes: Public graduate-lecture discussions of superspace, chiral actions, F-term breaking, the goldstino, and nonlinear sigma models were separated into new component and proof exercises. Solutions were independently derived and translated into the chapter's Majorana conventions.

sources.title: Supersymmetric Field Theory
sources.adaptation_notes: The official Part III lecture material on chiral superfields, F- and D-terms, Wess-Zumino models, nonlinear sigma models, and O'Raifeartaigh breaking informed new chapter-specific calculations. No source problem or solution text was reproduced.

sources.author_or_institution: Stephen P. Martin, Northern Illinois University
sources.title: A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.adaptation_notes: The verified version-7 sections on chiral Lagrangians, superspace, nonrenormalizable operators, and supersymmetry breaking were used to design independent dimensional-analysis and component exercises. All notation was converted to Volume III's conventional four-component formalism.
